platformDecision.hostingShape: HTTPS static hosting without an application backend

hard: A static-hostable browser build with no install step for the player
A deterministic and serializable social-state model testable without rendering
A stylized 3D port with readable thresholds, characters, schedules, picking and occlusion
Structured-data editing for identities, facts, permissions, memories and encounters
glTF-compatible replaceable assets behind stable asset IDs
Automated state tests, fixed checkpoints, build evidence and restart diagnostics
requirements.highestRiskUnknown: Whether identity-derived permissions and witness memory remain readable while navigating a 3D social space
requirements.cameraUnknown: First-person, close third-person and oblique overview remain candidates; the spike only uses an oblique overview and does not lock the camera.

evaluationModel.rule: weightedTotal = sum(score * weight); recommendation is evidence, not a human lock

candidates.label: Three.js + React Three Fiber + TypeScript
evidence: The isolated spike compiled 49 modules and produced a deployable static build.
Four deterministic model tests passed without mounting React or a renderer.
The development server returned HTTP 200 with the expected root document.
The existing repository toolchain contains the pinned packages, reducing setup uncertainty without making precedent the deciding criterion.
costsAndRisks: NPC schedules, navigation and editor tooling must be assembled rather than supplied as one integrated engine workflow.
The spike's initial JavaScript chunk is 1065.93 kB uncompressed / 296.19 kB gzip and triggers Vite's 500 kB warning.
No connected browser was available for visual or interactive verification in this run.
candidates.rejectionSignal: Reject if the next camera-and-threshold spike cannot keep the current claim, permission source and witness state readable without a bespoke editor-sized UI burden.

candidates.label: Babylon.js + TypeScript

route.renderer: Babylon.js WebGL2 with optional WebGPU path

evidence: Official specifications cover scene graphs, animation, collisions, picking, GUI, navigation/crowds, glTF and debugging tools.
The engine is browser-native and supports both WebGL and WebGPU routes.
costsAndRisks: This repository does not currently pin or validate the Babylon package route.
Switching adds a new rendering and interaction architecture before its bundle and deterministic integration have been spiked.
Its integrated capabilities could invite premature navigation, animation and editor scope.
candidates.reconsiderWhen: Prefer this route if the graybox proves that integrated NPC navigation, animation state machines and scene inspection outweigh the migration cost.

candidates.label: Godot 4 GDScript Web export

route.domain: GDScript resources and deterministic state services
route.deployment: WASM/PCK static hosting with required headers as configured

evidence: The scene editor, animation system, navigation and resource model fit a authored 3D social space.
Official Web export documentation supports browser delivery through the Compatibility renderer.
costsAndRisks: Godot 4 Web export is limited to the Compatibility renderer rather than Forward+ or Mobile renderers.
Threaded export requires cross-origin isolation; single-thread export improves compatibility but has performance tradeoffs.
The engine adds WASM/PCK delivery and a separate editor/runtime toolchain, making small code and UI iterations less reversible in this repository.
candidates.reconsiderWhen: Prefer this route if authored scene density, animation tooling and non-browser builds become more important than link-first iteration.

recommendation.oneSentence: Use a browser-native Three.js/R3F presentation over a pure TypeScript rules model because it proves the highest-risk architecture with the lowest migration cost while preserving an engine exit before visual production.
recommendation.whyNotLocked: Only the human can grant Tech Fit Lock.
initialExclusions: No physics package until a mechanic requires it
No runtime generative AI in authoritative game state
No WebGPU dependency for the first playable link
No formal art assets before Fun Lock and Visual Lock

spike.decisionDrivingClaim: The authoritative identity/fact/witness model can remain renderer-independent and deterministic while a browser-native 3D layer reacts to derived permissions.
spike.remainingRisk: Visual legibility and interaction were not observed in a connected browser.

portable: Pure TypeScript domain model and tests
Structured JSON content for identities, facts, permissions and schedules
Stable asset IDs and provenance records
migrationBoundary.lastCheapExit: Before Gate 3 asset production and before renderer-specific NPC/navigation code expands beyond the next graybox.
